license: Public domain (Library of Congress, Chronicling America); snapshot kept local only
imagesVia: official loc.gov JSON API (?fo=json) and IIIF image service; the HTML page shows a bot check to headless browsers, which we do not bypass
ocrReference: snapshots/<id>/images/ocr_alto.xml (the Library's own OCR; contains errors such as '1915' for 1912)
kind: historic newspaper front page scan: masthead, banner headline, map diagram, two halftone photos, stats table, 7 dense text columns

textView.deviceCheckOnly: the loc.gov viewer could not be captured headless (bot check); on the Monarch, check that the page image becomes an 'Explore tactile image' button and that 'Read page text' offers the text

pageText.headline: 1,340 PERISH AS TITANIC SINKS; ONLY 886, MOSTLY WOMEN AND CHILDREN, RESCUED
pageText.bodyMatch: loose: at most 10% word differences against the Library OCR after fixing its obvious errors
pageText.readingOrder: masthead, date line, headline, then columns left to right, each top to bottom; figure captions read with their figures

tactile.coordinateSpace: pixels of the 12.5% IIIF image [x0, y0, x1, y1]; tolerance 15 px

pageOverview1x.expect: three figures (map, captain photo, ship photo) and the stats table as outlined regions in place; masthead, headline and columns are touch regions without pins
pageOverview1x.deviceCheck: By touch: find the map at the top center and the two photos side by side below it.

shapes: coastline of North America and Newfoundland as one continuous outline
the Titanic's sinking position as a distinct small closed marker
other ships (Olympic, Carpathia, Parisian, Virginian, Californian, Baltic) as small markers
ship routes toward the wreck as lines (dashed lines become solid 1-pin lines)
drop: all printed labels as pins (they become component labels)
sea texture, smoke and halftone dots

shapes: the captain's outline: cap, bearded face, coat
the bridge window frame behind him
